= BITwiki Governance Framework: Distributed Intelligence Arbitration =

== Purpose ==

This document defines BITwiki's governance architecture—a recursive, self-regulating system for knowledge validation, quality arbitration, and community coordination. Unlike traditional wiki governance (Wikipedia's bureaucratic hierarchy, RationalWiki's elected moderators), BITwiki implements distributed intelligence arbitration where multiple agents (human and artificial) converge on truth through structured protocols.

== Core Principles ==

=== 1. Distributed Consensus ===

No single entity holds veto power. Decisions emerge from weighted convergence of multiple perspectives.

'''Weighting Factors:'''
* Epistemic reputation (track record of accurate contributions)
* Domain expertise (verified credentials or demonstrated knowledge)
* Recursion depth (engagement with feedback loops)
* Temporal stake (longevity in ecosystem)

=== 2. Transparent Arbitration ===

All governance actions are:
* Publicly logged with reasoning
* Subject to appeal and review
* Versioned with provenance tracking
* Machine-queryable via SMW

=== 3. Recursive Self-Regulation ===

Governance mechanisms themselves are subject to governance:
* Meta-governance protocols for rule changes
* Regular review of arbitration effectiveness
* Adaptive weighting based on outcomes

=== 4. Multi-Modal Validation ===

Claims require convergence across:
* Human expert review
* Algorithmic verification
* Community consensus
* Empirical evidence

== Governance Architecture ==

=== Layer 1: Constitutional Foundation ===

'''Scope:''' Immutable principles requiring unanimous consent
'''Change Process:''' Unanimous vote of all recognized stewards
'''Current Elements:'''
* Mission statement
* Core values (clarity, dignity, agency)
* Epistemic commitments
* Non-negotiable constraints

=== Layer 2: Structural Governance ===

'''Scope:''' Organizational mechanisms and processes
'''Change Process:''' 75% supermajority
'''Elements:'''
* Quality assessment frameworks
* Arbitration procedures
* Steward selection criteria
* Dispute resolution protocols

=== Layer 3: Operational Governance ===

'''Scope:''' Day-to-day decision making
'''Change Process:''' Simple majority or delegated authority
'''Elements:'''
* Content approval workflows
* Template modifications
* Category reorganizations
* Routine maintenance

== Quality Arbitration System ==

=== Epistemic Tier Assessment ===

| Tier | Criteria | Verification Required | Confidence |
|------|----------|----------------------|------------|
| Axiomatic | Self-evident or definitional | Logical verification | 1.0 |
| Established | Multiple peer-reviewed sources | Source verification | 0.85-0.99 |
| Supported | Single peer-reviewed + corroboration | Expert review | 0.70-0.84 |
| Working | Preliminary evidence, active research | Community review | 0.50-0.69 |
| Speculative | Hypothesis, limited evidence | Transparent marking | 0.20-0.49 |
| Disputed | Conflicting evidence | Controversy flagging | Variable |

=== Arbitration Process ===

'''Stage 1: Identification'''
* Automated flagging via quality metrics
* Community nomination
* Steward-initiated review

'''Stage 2: Evidence Gathering'''
* Source verification
* Expert consultation
* Cross-reference checking
* SMW property validation

'''Stage 3: Deliberation'''
* Structured discussion (minimum 7 days)
* Evidence presentation
* Counter-argument consideration
* Confidence scoring

'''Stage 4: Resolution'''
* Weighted vote by qualified arbiters
* Written reasoning required
* Appeal window (30 days)
* Implementation with version tracking

== Steward System ==

=== Steward Categories ===

'''Domain Stewards:'''
* Expertise in specific knowledge domains
* Authority within domain boundaries
* Cross-domain coordination required for boundary claims

'''Technical Stewards:'''
* SMW infrastructure maintenance
* Template and module development
* Quality metric implementation

'''Community Stewards:'''
* Conflict resolution
* Onboarding and education
* Cultural preservation

=== Steward Selection ===

'''Criteria:'''
* Demonstrated contribution quality
* Peer nomination (minimum 3)
* Knowledge assessment
* Values alignment verification

'''Process:'''
# Nomination period (30 days)
# Community feedback
# Steward council review
# Confirmation vote (66% threshold)
# Term limit: 2 years, renewable once

== Dispute Resolution ==

=== Dispute Categories ===

'''Epistemic Disputes:'''
* Conflicting evidence interpretations
* Source quality disagreements
* Confidence level assessments

'''Procedural Disputes:'''
* Process violations
* Arbitration fairness
* Steward conduct

'''Boundary Disputes:'''
* Scope definitions
* Category assignments
* Cross-domain claims

=== Resolution Pathways ===

'''Pathway A: Mediation'''
* Voluntary participation
* Neutral mediator assignment
* Non-binding recommendations

'''Pathway B: Arbitration Panel'''
* 3-5 member panel
* Binding decisions
* Written rationale required
* Appeal to full steward council

'''Pathway C: Constitutional Review'''
* Fundamental principle conflicts
* Full steward assembly
* Unanimous interpretation required

== Recursive Governance Metrics ==

=== Health Indicators ===

| Metric | Target | Measurement |
|--------|--------|-------------|
| Decision latency | < 14 days | Time from flag to resolution |
| Appeal rate | < 10% | Decisions challenged |
| Overturn rate | < 5% | Appeals successful |
| Participation | > 30% | Active community in governance |
| Quality drift | < 0.1 | Epistemic tier degradation |

=== Self-Correction Mechanisms ===

'''Quarterly Reviews:'''
* Arbitration effectiveness audit
* Steward performance evaluation
* Process efficiency analysis
* Community satisfaction survey

'''Annual Constitutional Convention:'''
* Structural governance amendments
* Steward system refinements
* Metric target adjustments
* Values reaffirmation

== SMW Integration ==

=== Governance Properties ===

```
[[Has steward::User:Name]]
[[Has domain::Domain Name]]
[[Has epistemic tier::Established]]
[[Has confidence::0.87]]
[[Has arbitration date::2026-02-13]]
[[Has decision type::Content Approval]]
[[Has vote count::12]]
[[Has approval rate::0.92]]
```

=== Query Patterns ===

'''Active Stewards:'''
{{#ask: [[Category:Steward]] [[Has status::Active]]
 |?Has domain
 |?Has term start
 |format=table
}}

'''Pending Arbitrations:'''
{{#ask: [[Category:Arbitration]] [[Has status::Pending]]
 |?Has submitter
 |?Has submission date
 |?Has domain
 |format=table
 |sort=Has submission date
 |order=asc
}}

'''Quality Metrics:'''
{{#ask: [[Category:Quality Assessment]]
 |?Has epistemic tier
 |?Has confidence
 |?Has verification date
 |format=table
 |sort=Has verification date
 |order=desc
}}

== Implementation Roadmap ==

=== Phase 1: Foundation (Months 1-3) ===
* Steward selection process
* Initial arbitration protocols
* SMW property implementation
* Community onboarding

=== Phase 2: Operation (Months 4-12) ===
* Active arbitration
* Metric collection
* Process refinement
* Dispute resolution

=== Phase 3: Optimization (Year 2+) ===
* Automated quality assessment
* Predictive dispute identification
* Recursive self-improvement
* Cross-wiki governance integration

== Conclusion ==

BITwiki's governance framework represents a third way between centralized control (Wikipedia) and pure anarchy. Through distributed intelligence arbitration, we achieve both quality and emergence—structured enough to maintain epistemic integrity, flexible enough to evolve with new knowledge.

The recursive nature ensures that governance itself is subject to governance, preventing ossification while maintaining stability. This is governance as a living system—not a machine to be built, but a garden to be cultivated.
